name: Floor & Transmission/Driveshaft Tunnel
description: The central tunnel housing the transmission tail, driveshaft and exhaust, its bolt-on underbody brace, driveshaft safety loop, body plugs and tunnel heat protection.

components.name: Transmission / driveshaft tunnel
components.description: Raised center section of the floor that houses the TR-6060 (or 10L90) transmission tail, the driveshaft and the dual exhaust. It is a key torsional member. Race builds may need local clearancing for larger exhaust, a dry-sump-related engine setback, or a sequential/transaxle swap; any cut must be boxed back in to restore stiffness.
components.location: Car centerline, x approx 0.7-2.6, y approx 0.18-0.45.

factory.name: GM stamped steel tunnel
factory.notes: Shifter opening and transmission crossmember mounting points are in the tunnel.

raceOptions.name: Clearanced and re-boxed tunnel (fabricated)
raceOptions.notes: Use 16-18 ga steel to box in any relief; seam weld all new panels.

installNotes: Mock up transmission, driveshaft, exhaust and shifter before any tunnel modification.
Maintain at least 25 mm (1 in) between exhaust and the tunnel/fuel or brake lines, or add heat shielding.
inspection: Check tunnel around transmission mount for cracking.

modelRef.features: Pressed inverted-U tunnel with sloped walls, flanges and beads

components.name: Driveshaft tunnel brace (underbody brace)
components.description: Bolt-on brace spanning the open bottom of the tunnel beneath the driveshaft, bolted to the floor pan with 5 bolts. Closes the tunnel section for torsional stiffness and serves as the mounting for an aftermarket driveshaft safety loop.
components.location: Under the tunnel behind the transmission, approx x 1.4-1.7, y approx 0.17, z 0.

factory.name: GM factory tunnel brace
factory.notes: Retained with 5 bolts (13 mm hex) into the floor.

raceOptions.name: BMR DTB005 (steel) / DTB006 (aluminum) driveshaft tunnel brace
raceOptions.notes: Bolts to factory holes using factory hardware; two aluminum spacer washers go under the front two bolts.

hardware.notes: Value from BMR instructions using factory hardware.

installNotes: Install after exhaust and driveshaft are in (phase 6) but plan the holes during floor prep.
inspection: Check bolts and look for exhaust heat damage.

modelRef.features: Bolt-in bridge across the tunnel opening

components.name: Driveshaft safety loop
components.description: Steel hoop around the front section of the driveshaft that catches the shaft if a U-joint/CV or coupler fails. Required by many sanctioning bodies for cars with high-power front-engine RWD layouts (check NASA/SCCA class rules). Gen 6 aftermarket loops attach to the factory tunnel brace.
components.location: Around driveshaft near front, x approx 1.4, y approx 0.35, z 0.

raceOptions.name: BMR DSL019 driveshaft safety loop
raceOptions.notes: Attaches to the factory driveshaft tunnel brace.

specs.Clearance: Maintain >= 12 mm (1/2 in) around shaft at full drivetrain movement

hardware.notes: Follow kit instructions if they differ.

installNotes: Check clearance with drivetrain rocked on its mounts.
inspection: Look for witness marks indicating shaft contact.

sources.title: BMR 6th gen Camaro product line overview

modelRef.features: Steel strap hoop around the driveshaft bolted to the tunnel

components.name: Body plugs, drain plugs and pass-through grommets
components.description: Rubber/plastic plugs closing factory drain and access holes in floor, rockers and trunk, plus grommets for every line or harness pass-through. Missing plugs let fumes and water into the cockpit; class rules generally require the cockpit to be sealed from the engine, fuel and track surface.
components.location: Floor pan, rockers, trunk floor, dash panel.

raceOptions.name: Aluminum pop-rivet / weld-in plugs for unused holes
raceOptions.notes: Weld-in steel discs are stronger and do not fall out.

installNotes: Plug all unused holes after paint; leave drain holes in rockers open or plugged per your corrosion strategy.
inspection: Check for missing plugs (exhaust fumes in cockpit).

components.name: Tunnel and floor heat shielding
components.description: Reflective/insulating barrier on the tunnel and floor above the exhaust and transmission. Factory stamped aluminum shields are often discarded in a race build; replace with lightweight reflective heat barrier to protect the driver, seat, lines and harnesses.
components.location: Tunnel underside and floor near exhaust, x approx 0.8-2.6.

factory.name: GM stamped aluminum underbody heat shields

raceOptions.name: Self-adhesive reflective heat barrier
raceOptions.notes: Apply to clean, painted surface; add mechanical fasteners near the exhaust.

installNotes: Apply after paint and after line/harness routing is final.

modelRef.features: Embossed aluminium shield under the tunnel roof
